Title: TH recovers bonuses paid to Properties board members [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Efforts to recover bonuses paid to members of the Tabung Haji Properties board have already been carried out following findings by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji (TH).
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the recovery was among the recommendations already implemented, accounting for 75 per cent of the RCI's recommendations.
Winding up the debate on the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today, he said the RCI had also identified weaknesses in the valuation and financial reporting methods used to determine TH's financial position from 2014 to 2017.
This included the use of the "realisable asset value", which resulted in the institution's financial position appearing better than its actual condition.
Zulkifli said the RCI's findings had subsequently formed the basis for strengthening internal controls, financial reporting and accountability within TH.
On bonuses of up to 13 months, he said the RCI found weaknesses in the assessment of the institution's financial position, highlighting the need to ensure remuneration and incentives were aligned with its actual performance.
"The RCI shows that there were weaknesses in the assessment of the financial position that need to be improved so that rewards and incentives are in line with the actual performance of the institution," he said.
Zulkifli also said there had previously been no specific policy limiting the number of companies in which an individual could simultaneously serve as a nominee director.
He said this highlighted the need to strengthen policies on conflicts of interest, limits on appointments and oversight to ensure responsibilities could be carried out effectively.
"These have also been implemented based on the recommendations of the RCI," he said.
The 211-page RCI report revealed governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in investment fair value.
It also found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the reported RM3.4 billion profit, had Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) been fully applied.

Title: 5 Bank Negara warning letters on Tabung Haji to be referred to PM, cabinet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Proposals to release five Bank Negara Malaysia warning letters and other documents linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji will be referred to the prime minister and cabinet.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said this in response to calls by several MPs for the government to release the documents to help MPs and the public better understand the issues uncovered by the RCI.
The documents sought included five warning letters issued by Bank Negara to Tabung Haji, the Roland Berger report, minutes of meetings concerning changes to impairment policies and minutes relating to the approval of hibah distributions.
"Regarding the proposal to release all five Bank Negara warning letters, the Roland Berger report, minutes of meetings on changes to impairment policies and minutes relating to the approval of hibah, this matter will be referred to the prime minister and the Cabinet," he said when winding up the debate on the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Earlier, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) supported calls for the release of the RCI's exhibits and appendices.
He said making the supporting documents available would enable Malaysians to better understand the evidence and issues examined by the commission.
Zulkifli said the government took note of the proposal and would consider the matter.
The RCI report identified weaknesses in Tabung Haji's governance and financial management, including issues concerning its financial reporting and assessment of its financial position.
Zulkifli said the government had since taken steps to strengthen Tabung Haji's governance and regulatory framework, with 19 of the RCI's 25 recommendations, or 75 per cent, already implemented.
The remaining six recommendations are in various stages of implementation, including amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995, strengthening regulatory oversight, improving disciplinary procedures and reviewing policies relating to deposits, haj payments and financial assistance.

Title: RMAF, IAF test interoperability in Udara Shakti 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian and Indian fighter jets are taking part in a five-day air exercise aimed at improving interoperability between the two air forces.
The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) has deployed Sukhoi Su-30MKMs and F/A-18D Hornets, while the Indian Air Force (IAF) is taking part with Dassault Rafales in Exercise Udara Shakti 2026 (US 26).
The exercise began yesterday and runs until Friday, with 83 officers and personnel from both air forces involved. The flying phase runs from today until Thursday.
In a Facebook post, the RMAF said it had deployed two Su-30MKM fighters from No. 12 Squadron, two F/A-18D fighters from No. 18 Squadron and an Airbus A400M transport aircraft from No. 8 Squadron.
"The IAF has brought four Rafale fighters from 101 Squadron and two Boeing C-17 Globemaster III strategic transport aircraft from 81 Squadron.
"The flying phase features dissimilar basic fighter manoeuvres (DBFM), dissimilar air combat training (DACT), air-to-air refuelling (AAR) and aerial photography, or PHOTEX," it said.
The drills are aimed at testing how effectively the two air forces can operate different fighter platforms together, including their procedures, operational coordination, communications systems and logistical support.
They will also test aircrews' ability to make rapid and accurate decisions while planning and executing complex air missions.
The exercise officially opened at the Air Warfare Centre Auditorium at Subang Air Base, where RMAF exercise director Colonel Shamsul Shahreen Isa and IAF exercise director Group Captain Parijat Jha jointly officiated the ceremony through the symbolic pinning of the exercise patch.
Also present was Indian Defence Adviser to Malaysia Colonel Praveen Sukumaran.
US 26 is a biennial bilateral air exercise between the RMAF and IAF, conducted during the Indian air force's transit through Malaysia following its participation in Exercise Pitch Black 2026 in Australia.
Beyond the flying component, a Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) session will also provide a platform for both air forces to share knowledge, expertise and operational experience.
"Discussions will cover exercise development, collective training concepts, integrated operations, training doctrine, scenario planning and the use of science and technology in modern military training.
"The exchange is expected to allow both air forces to share best practices and refine training methods, while exposure to different aircraft capabilities and operational characteristics will enhance aircrews' adaptability in an increasingly complex and dynamic air warfare environment," the RMAF said.
US 26 also serves as a platform for defence diplomacy between Malaysia and India, strengthening trust, mutual understanding and professional ties between their armed forces.

Title: Explained: Kedah’s bid to stop lotteries reaches Federal Court today; here’s what it’s about
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Kedah state government is asking the Federal Court today to allow it to proceed with its appeals, with the ultimate goal of stopping lotteries from operating in the state.
Known variously as “toto”, “4D”, “kedai empat nombor ekor”, number forecast operators or pool betting businesses, these lottery operators have been unable to open their physical outlets in Kedah since 2023 despite holding federal business licences.
Previously on December 12, 2025, the Court of Appeal had in a 2-1 decision said the Kedah state government had acted unconstitutionally, unlawfully and irrationally when it decided to not renew the physical outlets’ premises licences for these lotteries starting from 2023.
The Court of Appeal’s decision overturned Kedah’s refusal to renew the premises licences and upheld an order for the courts to assess the compensation amounts for losses arising from the non-renewals.
The Kedah state government wants to appeal this, but it has to first get leave or permission from the Federal Court for the appeal to be heard.
The Kedah government is expected to argue today that its appeal at the Federal Court should proceed based on six questions of law, while the lottery companies are expected to argue that the state government should not get leave to continue its appeal.
Here’s
Malay Mail
’s simplified summary about previous court decisions in this case and what it is actually about, based on the Court of Appeal judgments and other court documents:
What this case is not about
In short, the case is not about whether gambling should be allowed, but whether Kedah had exceeded its constitutional powers by encroaching on matters under the federal government.
Court of Appeal judge Datuk Faizah Jamaludin said the case did not concern unlicensed gambling, nor was the court being asked to decide whether gambling was socially or morally desirable.
She made clear that the lottery companies were not asking the court to decide whether Kedah should approve of gambling.
Faizah instead said the court has to decide a constitutional and public law question, which is whether the Kedah state government’s decision — implemented by refusing to give premises licences to all pool betting businesses in the state — can be used to impose a state-wide ban on these federally-licensed pool betting businesses.
Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak (CJSS) Datuk Azizah Nawawi, who was also on the Court of Appeal panel, had said this case is not about rights to gamble.
Instead, she said the only issue is whether the Kedah state government’s decision to stop issuing premises licences for pool betting businesses within the state is “ultra vires” or beyond its authority under the Federal Constitution.
Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor in 2021 announced that the state would not renew licences for the premises or physical outlets used by lotteries. — Bernama file pic
Chronology of key events
On November 14, 2021, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor announced that the Kedah government had decided to no longer renew premises licences for lotteries or gaming outlets in Kedah.
On December 8, 2021, the Kedah government (via the Kedah MB and state exco) in a meeting noted that the Finance Ministry had approved gambling licences for lotteries and their agents in Kedah from January 1 to December 31, 2022.
The Kedah government in that meeting decided on three things:
agreed that the Finance Ministry should no longer consider renewing gambling licences in Kedah for 2023 since such licence applications were under the ministry;
all premises licences for number forecast operators in Kedah will end on December 31, 2022 in line with the Finance Ministry’s gambling licences ending on that date;
Kedah’s local councils and the police would carry out strict enforcement if any lotteries continue operating after December 31, 2022 in Kedah.
From November 2022 to January 2023, Kedah’s local councils in Kedah issued letters to the lotteries’ operators, informing them of the Kedah state government’s decision and also informing them that their premises licences would not be renewed starting January 1, 2023.
While some of the premises licences would only expire in 2023, these lotteries or pool betting businesses could not continue operating, as the local councils had said enforcement action would be taken if they continue operating after December 31, 2022.
Based on court documents, the Finance Minister actually did renew the annual pool betting licences for these lottery companies and their agents for January 1 to December 31, 2023.
So what happened was the lottery companies had the licence from the federal government to run their business, but they could not use the physical outlets or premises in Kedah.
The practical effect or result was they could no longer do business in Kedah.
Some of them had been running their business at their premises in Kedah for many years, with the earliest one since 1988.
File picture of a lottery ticket with the words ‘Judi Adalah Haram Di Sisi Agama Islam’ printed on its back. — Picture by Hari Anggara
Based on court documents including licence documents, the Finance Ministry imposes a list of conditions for pool betting licences, such as requiring “Judi Adalah Haram Di Sisi Agama Islam” (Gambling is forbidden in Islam) to be printed on each lottery ticket.
Another condition requires signboards to be placed outside the lottery ticket counters with these messages:
“Judi Adalah Haram Di Sisi Agama Islam”;
both Muslims and those aged below 21 are not allowed to enter the premises.
Other conditions include requiring pool betting licence holders to ensure those aged below 21 and Muslims do not enter the place where lottery tickets are sold, as well as not allowing Muslims to be number forecast ticket or lottery ticket sellers.
File picture of a lottery shop in Selangor, with a sign at the lottery ticket counter stating the messages as required by the Finance Ministry as conditions for the annual pool betting business licence. — Picture by Hari Anggara
Total six cases
In 2023, lottery or pool betting companies STM Lottery Sdn Bhd (Sports Toto Berhad’s wholly-owned subsidiary) and ENE (Penang) Sdn Bhd (a regional office of Magnum 4D Bhd), their officers, and pool betting agents filed separate court challenges against Kedah’s refusal to renew their outlets’ premises licences there.
Six court challenges were filed via judicial review, with those named as respondents being the Kedah government, the Kedah menteri besar, the Alor Setar City Council and its mayor, the Sungai Petani Municipal Council and its president, the Baling district council and its president.
On October 17, 2023, the High Court only granted leave for the court challenges to be heard against the Kedah government.
What happened at the High Court in Alor Setar, Kedah
On June 20, 2024, High Court judge Mahazan Mat Taib decided in the lottery companies and agents’ favour for all six cases that were heard together, granting four orders:
a declaration that the Kedah government had acted illegally and irrationally (through its December 8, 2021 decision and by causing the local councils to issue those letters);
a declaration that the Kedah government’s decision is unconstitutional, null and void;
Kedah government’s decision is quashed, and that the court would assess how much it has to pay as compensation for the companies’ losses.
The High Court decision did not make any court orders regarding the Kedah MB, but the Kedah MB had together with the Kedah government appealed against both the High Court and Court of Appeal decisions.
What the Court of Appeal said
In her 25-page judgment, Court of Appeal judge Faizah agreed with the High Court’s decision, noting that the Kedah government had crossed over into the federal government’s powers to regulate lotteries.
This is because the Federal Constitution places “betting and lotteries” under the federal government’s law-making powers, while “local government” comes under the state governments’ law-making powers.
This would enable local authorities or local councils to regulate the use of business premises, public order, sanitation, safety, nuisance, suitability of location and other genuinely local factors.
Faizah said a local authority cannot use its power to regulate premises to prohibit an activity that comes under federal licence.
But in this case, the local councils’ letters did not identify defects, safety, sanitation, planning or nuisance reasons in any of the premises for the lottery outlets, and had instead referred to the state’s decision to stop issuing or renewing their premises licences from January 1, 2023.
In other words, the blanket refusal to give premises licences to these betting and lottery businesses throughout Kedah was not due to any defect in the premises or actually about regulating premises, but was purely because of disapproval of such activities and has the effect of prohibiting a federally-licensed activity.
Faizah said this does not mean every refusal of a premises licence to a pool betting operator is unconstitutional.
The judge said a local council can still refuse to give a premises licence if there are genuine and legitimate reasons, such as planning, zoning, safety, public health, nuisance, traffic, building non-compliance, or other matters that come under local governments.
Court of Appeal judge Datuk Lim Hock Leng, who agreed with Faizah and the High Court, said it is unconstitutional for a state to prohibit pool betting businesses (which is exclusively under the federal government’s regulation) by not renewing business premises licences.
In a 25-page judgment, Lim said the Kedah government’s decision violates the Federal Constitution’s Article 81, where every state shall exercise its executive authority without impeding or obstructing the federal government’s exercise of its federal authority.
CJSS Azizah disagreed with the other judges’ conclusion that the Kedah government’s decision was unconstitutional, irrational and illegal.
In her 70-page minority judgment, Azizah said the Kedah state exco’s decision is not “ultra vires” or stepping beyond the state’s powers under the Federal Constitution, as non-renewal of business premises licences comes under states’ law-making powers.
Azizah also said that the court cannot review or decide the court challenge on the Kedah government’s decision to not renew premise licences for all lotteries in the state, as she viewed it as a “policy” decided by the state government.

Title: Beyond rockets: MYSA wants Malaysians to see how space tech shapes daily life
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — Space technology must be made accessible so that the public understands its applications go beyond rockets, satellites or astronauts, as it has become an essential part of everyday management and daily life.
Malaysian Space Agency (MYSA) director-general Datuk Azlikamil Napiah said the ‘Space for All’ aspiration means that space technology should be accessible, understood and utilised by all segments of society.
“My aspiration is to see space technology brought closer to the people. We are already using it every day, but many are unaware of it. Telephone communication networks, television broadcasts, navigation applications such as Waze, as well as delivery service operations largely rely on space technology, particularly satellites,” he told Bernama recently.
He said public awareness of space technology is crucial to encourage the development of more operable systems or solution-based applications that can meet the actual needs of the people.
Azlikamil said as society becomes more aware of its benefits, demand for new application systems will increase, thereby driving innovation, expertise, industry growth and the development of the local space ecosystem.
He said space technology is not limited to observing outer space, but also helps humans manage life and resources on Earth through advanced systems such as communication satellites, navigation and remote sensing.
Satellite data, he said, can be utilised across various sectors including agriculture, fisheries, public health, disaster management, environmental monitoring, natural resource management and food security.
For example, Azlikamil said remote sensing technology enables padi cultivation areas and farming operations to be monitored more systematically. Soil fertility can also be identified, and harvest yields predicted, helping the government plan food supply needs and channel subsidies in a more targeted manner.
He added that the same technology is also used to identify potential groundwater sources, monitor floods, open burning, illegal waste disposal, deforestation activities and areas at risk of dengue outbreaks.
“Space technology supports three main aspects, which are planning, monitoring and mitigation. The information obtained enables faster and more accurate analysis and data-driven decision-making,” he said.
He also shared that to date, MYSA has collaborated with about 90 government agencies and developed up to 65 solution-based application systems using space technology tailored to their needs.
However, Azlikamil said the adoption of advanced space technology still faces challenges, as some parties remain more comfortable with conventional methods.
As such, he said MYSA develops applications based on the demands and needs of user agencies to ensure the technologies developed are utilised effectively and deliver optimal benefits.
“There is no point in developing sophisticated solutions if no one uses them or if they have no impact. Technology must be fully leveraged to solve real problems faced by the people and the nation,” he said.
He added that space technology also opens up career opportunities for the younger generation that are beyond astronomy or the astronaut profession.
He said the space sector ecosystem encompasses various disciplines including engineering, data analysis, space law, software development, component manufacturing, robotics and automation, as well as Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
Azlikamil said greater awareness of space technology will help Malaysia develop skilled talents, produce local innovations and ensure their benefits are enjoyed by all.
“Space technology is no longer something exclusive as it once was. Our goal is to ensure it is used to enhance the people’s well-being and simplify the management of daily life,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Finance Minister II: Seven of Tabung Haji’s 14 troubled investments ended in total losses, Saudi-based deal caused biggest hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Seven of the 14 troubled investments involving Tabung Haji identified by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) resulted in total losses, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Amir Hamzah said that among the seven, investments linked to Saudi Arabia-based property development and management firm Al-Rawda Real Estates Development recorded the highest losses.
From 2015 to 2017, Tabung Haji reportedly paid RM1.5 billion as part of a lease deal with Al-Rawda involving four hotels in Madinah designated to house haj pilgrims from Malaysia.
Amir Hamzah said that despite Al-Rawda failing to provide a bank guarantee or complete due diligence, Tabung Haji entered into the deal, relying only on an individual’s personal note.
He, however, did not name the individual.
“Al-Rawda began defaulting on its rent payments for Tabung Haji since the first quarter of 2019, leading to RM1.86 billion in losses as of 2024,” Amir Hamzah said during his winding-up speech on the Tabung Haji RCI report today.
