Title: ‘Let’s work together’: Sabah Fire Dept urges public to avoid open burning amid transboundary haze
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 11 — The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has urged the public to stop open burning as transboundary haze from Kalimantan, Indonesia, has begun to affect air quality in the state.
Its director Mohd Pisar Aziz said haze had begun to cover areas including Kota Kinabalu and Kimanis following forest fires in the neighbouring region.
“Winds from southern and central Borneo are carrying thick smoke towards northern Borneo, affecting visibility and air quality in Sabah.
“Hot and dry weather also increases the risk of fires. Let us work together to prevent them, protect lives, property and the environment, as open burning is an offence,” he told Bernama today.
A check on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) this afternoon showed that air quality in Sabah remained at the moderate level, with Kota Kinabalu recording the highest reading at 83, followed by Politeknik Kota Kinabalu at 81 and Kimanis at 76.
Mohd Pisar said high-risk groups, including asthma patients, children and the elderly, should take extra precautions despite the moderate API readings.
He said Keningau and Pitas had also recorded seven consecutive days without rain up to August 10, meeting the criteria for an open-burning ban.
The ban covers the open burning of rubbish, dry leaves, garden waste, construction waste and other materials that could worsen the haze, he said.
The public is advised to limit outdoor activities between 11am and 4pm, stay hydrated, wear face masks in hazy areas, and regularly check electrical wiring to prevent fires.
They should also avoid discarding cigarette butts carelessly and immediately report any suspicious activities or fires to JBPM via 999. — Bernama

Title: Former High Court judge’s driver jailed three after pleading guilty to criminal intimidation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The former driver of a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge was sentenced to three months’ jail by the Magistrate’s Court here today for criminally intimidating the judge last May.
Magistrate Heng Yi Min handed down the sentence after Mohd Fareez Mohd Zin, 39, changed his plea to guilty during today’s case mention.
According to the charge, he is accused of committing the offence against High Court Judge Gan Techiong, 64, with the intention of causing fear and alarm to the judge at the Kuala Lumpur High Court (Civil) complex, Jalan Duta, here, at 1.30pm on May 8.
The charge, under Section 506 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or bot.
According to the facts of the case, Mohd Fareez sent two threatening voice recordings via WhatsApp and made a phone call to Gan’s secretary.
In the voice recording, the accused allegedly made defamatory statements and threats against the judge.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Iman Nurhidayah Ezani urged the court to impose a sentence commensurate with the seriousness of the offence.
“The offence is serious and could jeopardise the reputation and safety of the complainant, even though no physical injury was caused. A proportionate sentence must be imposed to serve as a deterrent to the accused and society as a whole,” she said.
Counsel Shah Rizal Abdul Manan, representing the accused, appealed for a lighter sentence, citing his client’s responsibility to support three children and an unemployed wife. — Bernama

Title: RoS to scrutinise Bersatu complaint over Perikatan membership status
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has confirmed receiving an official complaint from Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) over claims that the party was not involved in the Perikatan Nasional (PN) Supreme Council meeting on July 16 and issues related to its membership in the coalition.
RoS said in a statement today that it was examining the complaint received today, based on the Societies Act 1966 [Act 832], the Societies Regulations 1984, the organisation's approved constitution, and the department's official records.
“To ensure that the review is comprehensive and based on the law, all information, documents and explanations submitted by the parties concerned will be examined.
“The issues raised will be reviewed based on the provisions of the law currently in force,” RoS said in the statement today.
In carrying out its responsibility, RoS said it would continue to act professionally and impartially and had no interest in any organisation or political party.
RoS also stressed that every registered organisation must comply with the Societies Act 1966, relevant regulations and its respective constitution.
Earlier, the media reported that Bersatu planned to lodge a report with RoS over claims by other quarters that its membership in PN would automatically cease following the party's intention to form a new political coalition. — Bernama

Title: Drug smuggling via KLIA: 14 Malaysians arrested abroad since January, say police
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A total of 14 Malaysians have been arrested overseas for alleged drug smuggling activities after departing on outbound flights from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between January and July this year, federal narcotics police said today.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 14 Malaysians comprised 11 men and three women, with Taiwan recording the highest number of arrests at six.
The remaining arrests involved three in Indonesia, two in the Philippines and one each in Hong Kong, Macau and the Maldives, with a total of 73.17kg of drugs worth RM5.5 million seized.
In contrast, Hussein said federal police successfully thwarted drug smuggling activities at KLIA during the same period, arresting 51 individuals and seizing a total of 1.2 tonnes of drugs worth RM97 million.
The majority of those arrested held British passports (14 people), followed by Malaysians (12), Singaporeans (eight) and French nationals (five).
Indonesia, Hong Kong and Japan each accounted for two nationals, while Thailand, Ireland, Slovakia, India, Portugal and Uganda each accounted for one.
“So, if we compare both statistics — those who ‘escaped’ and were arrested overseas — it accounts for about seven per cent of the total arrests we made in foiling drug smuggling attempts at KLIA, which shows that we are doing a good job,” he told a press conference at the Selangor contingent headquarters.
Hussein said the Royal Malaysia Police has consistently highlighted drug seizures at press conferences to raise public awareness and prevent Malaysians from falling victim to syndicates offering various travel incentives or payments to lure them into transporting drugs.

Title: Police bust syndicate storing RM21m worth of ganja near KLIA, Penang airport
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — Federal narcotics police foiled an international drug syndicate’s tactic of storing ganja flowers supplied from neighbouring countries at residences near international airports before they were transported by drug mules, following the arrest of nine individuals earlier this month.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the arrests were the result of a month-long operation from July 12 to August 3 aimed at crippling a drug distribution network transporting drugs to Europe.
“The syndicate’s modus operandi was to temporarily store the ganja flowers obtained via our northern neighbour at terrace houses near Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas and Kuala Lumpur International Airport near Nilai, Negeri Sembilan.
“The drugs would then be handed over to various drug mules recruited and exploited by the syndicate.
“The overall drug seizure weighed 270.27kg, with an estimated value of RM21.62 million, enough to supply some 630,000 users,” he told a press conference at the Selangor police headquarters here.
He said that of the nine arrested in three separate police raids, five were Portuguese nationals, two were Singaporeans, and one each was Malaysian and Burmese.
All those arrested were aged between 22 and 51, and are believed to have acted as drug mules, coordinators, transporters and syndicate members.
Hussein said the first police raid on July 12 in front of a hotel lobby in Bayan Lepas led to the arrest of three suspects and the seizure of 290 packages of ganja flowers stored at residences and in luggage in Penang and Mantin, Negeri Sembilan.
Following the initial raid, police arrested six more suspects around Sepang, Selangor, and Bayan Lepas on August 3, seizing an additional 60 packages of ganja flowers.
“This latest success is a testament to our commitment to dismantling an international drug distribution syndicate using Malaysia as a transit route to smuggle ganja flowers overseas,” he said.

Title: Five motorcycles seized after man repeatedly caught for extreme modifications
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The actions of a man who spent up to RM25,000 to extremely modify five motorcycles backfired when all the vehicles were confiscated by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) after he was detained five times since last year.
What is more shocking is that the actions of the individual, who is in his 20s, also affected his family members, as four of the five motorcycles belonged to his father, younger sibling, mother, and uncle, which he had borrowed before modifying them.
JPJ Senior Director of Enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the fifth motorcycle belonging to the self-employed man was detained during JPJ’s Op Ekstrem around the capital recently for offences involving the modification of engine structures, braking systems, and the use of components not complying with safety specifications.
“In previous press conferences, I used a firm approach, but this time I want to appeal to these ‘hardcore’ riders to stop taking these useless actions.
“Imagine, the five motorcycles we detained and are holding in our custody belong to himself, his uncle, his aunt, his father, and most recently, his younger sibling’s motorcycle. All five of these motorcycles are currently in the process of forfeiture and will be auctioned off,” he said at a press conference here.
Muhammad Kifli said extreme modification offences such as removing the rear brakes, using ‘tayar sotong’ (pencil tires), changing the Electronic Control Unit (ECU), and modifying engines not only endanger lives but also increases the risk of fatal road accidents.
He said that throughout Op Ekstrem conducted on August 8 and 9, a total of 443 motorcycles were inspected, with 336 of them acted against and 140 motorcycles confiscated.
“Overall, for the period from January to August 10 this year, JPJ has carried out 441 Op Ekstrem operations nationwide, which saw inspections on 68,528 vehicles, with 18,534 of them subjected to enforcement actions and 1,942 vehicles confiscated,” he said.
He added that JPJ will not hesitate to take legal action under Section 59(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) against any party that refuses to restore their vehicles to their original specifications.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Kifli informed that JPJ will hold its first engagement session with the organisers of RXZ Members to discuss safety aspects and the smooth organisation of the programme in the future.
“Our purpose to hold this engagement session is not to restrict the organisation of the programme, but rather to listen to the organisers’ views and provide suggestions for improvement to ensure that the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and the safety of all road users are complied with.”
The meeting is scheduled to take place at 2:30 pm at the JPJ Headquarters in Putrajaya tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin urges govt to complete forensic audit of Tabung Haji funds within a year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Pagoh MP Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has urged the government to immediately conduct a comprehensive and transparent forensic audit of the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) funds and complete it within a year.
The former prime minister said the move was important following weaknesses in governance and transparency in the management of TH funds, as revealed in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
“An independent forensic audit is crucial to trace the flow of funds, identify elements of fraud, abuse of power and possible negligence.
“Anyone responsible for causing losses to TH funds, whether through fraud, abuse of power or negligence, must be brought to justice,” he said during the debate on the TH RCI report at the Special Dewan Rakyat Sitting today.
Muhyiddin, who is also Bersatu president, said the findings in the report, which among others revealed that TH recorded estimated cumulative losses of between RM10 billion and RM12.6 billion from 2014 to 2020, must be taken seriously and followed by firm action without compromise.
Meanwhile, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) urged the government to establish a Multi-Agency Task Force to investigate 14 problematic TH investments identified in the RCI report.
He said the task force should involve several enforcement agencies, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), police and the Inland Revenue Board, to ensure investigations were conducted comprehensively rather than in silos.
“The government needs to announce the establishment of a Multi-Agency Task Force to investigate each of the 14 investments that have been proven problematic, and extend the scope to Felda, FGV and Eagle High.
“So that ultimately we can find out who caused these problems and establish the losses that resulted,” he said, adding that he also proposed forensic audits of the problematic investments.
Echoing him, Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) proposed that MACC, police and relevant enforcement agencies provide regular updates, within a clearly defined timeframe, on all investigations arising from the RCI findings.
Hasni also proposed that today’s special sitting mark the beginning of continuous, bipartisan and institution-based parliamentary oversight to ensure the implementation of all RCI recommendations is regularly monitored and reported to the Dewan Rakyat.
The special sitting provides MPs with an opportunity to examine the TH RCI report, which was made public on July 29 after the government decided that its findings should be made known to the people.
The report contains various findings concerning weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, as well as 25 recommendations for improvement, of which 75 per cent had been implemented by TH as of July 30. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman sends narcotics team to Jakarta to question Malaysian pilot held with 26kg ecstasy
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A team of officers from the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department has arrived in Indonesia to question a Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport last month.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team of four arrived earlier today and has been given two days, August 12 to 13, to interrogate the suspect.
“The interrogation will involve obtaining further detailed information from the suspect to compare with our findings here,” he told a press conference at the Selangor contingent headquarters.
Hussein said investigators were tracing the alleged syndicate members but faced some difficulties because the phone numbers used for communication were registered under false or inaccurate identities.
He also said that four to five individuals have been called in for questioning so far to determine if an insider was involved in the case.
“We are satisfied with the statement provided but it is still too early for me to reveal whether an insider was involved without solid evidence to prove it.
“Yet at the same time I do not rule out such a possibility,” he said.
The case involves a 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot who was arrested shortly after arriving at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport from Kuala Lumpur on July 28.
Indonesian authorities said more than 26kg of ecstasy tablets and a small quantity of methamphetamine were found in a suitcase the pilot collected after customs officers flagged it during an X-ray inspection.

Title: Police detain eight over suspected murder of man at Kuala Langat oil palm plantation
Article:
KUALA LANGAT, Aug 11 — Police are investigating the death of a man believed to have been murdered at an oil palm plantation in Sungai Kelambu, Banting here last Sunday.
Kuala Langat District Police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi, in a statement, said eight individuals had been arrested to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“At about 5 pm on Aug 9, a policeman on duty reported that a 49-year-old local man was found unconscious at an oil palm plantation,” he said in a statement today.
Akmalrizal also urged members of the public with information to go to the nearest police station or contact the Kuala Langat District Police Headquarters Operations Room at 03-3187 2222.
Meanwhile, all the suspects, including foreigners aged between 20 and 60, have been remanded for seven days to assist investigations following a remand order issued by Magistrate Maslinda Selamat. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Police officers must keep evolving as security landscape grows more dynamic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has urged all police officers to think critically, act swiftly and remain relevant amid changing times to meet the challenges of an increasingly dynamic policing landscape.
He said the ever-changing security landscape required continuous evolution, and officers should not become complacent with their current positions or achievements.
“Promotion is not the pinnacle of a career, but rather the starting point of far greater and more challenging responsibilities,” he said at the Police Senior Officers’ Rank Insignia and Honorary Rank Insignia Presentation Ceremony at the Senior Police Officers’ Mess, Bukit Aman here today.
Mohd Khalid said the rank held by an officer represented a trust placed by the people and the country, which must be shouldered with transparency, wisdom and sincerity to ensure peace and security were maintained.
A total of 29 senior police officers were honoured at the ceremony for their promotions to the ranks of Commissioner of Police (CP), Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Senior Assistant Commissioner (SAC) and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP).
The ceremony also saw honorary ranks conferred on three individuals, reflecting the Royal Malaysia Police’s (PDRM) strategy to build an extensive network of cooperation.
They were Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibuddeen, who received the Honorary ACP rank, while Aini Suraya Osman and Adila Abdullah were each conferred the Honorary Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) rank.  — Bernama

Title: PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim says lawyers handling Anwar’s defamation suit
Article:
KOTA BARU, Aug 11 — PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he would leave it to his lawyers to respond to the defamation suit filed against him by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Kubang Kerian MP said the remarks at the centre of the suit were general in nature and had also been raised by other parties and sources, the
New Straits Times
reported.
“I have handed the matter over to my lawyers to take the necessary action.
“What I stated was something general, which has also been mentioned by many parties and from various sources,” he said.
Anwar filed the suit at the High Court on Monday over remarks Tuan Ibrahim allegedly made during a political speech at Felda Jenderak Utara, Kuala Krau, Pahang, on or about June 14.
Anwar’s lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the statements were false and defamatory of the Prime Minister.
He said the case also concerned the alleged publication and republication of the remarks through video recordings and social media platforms, including YouTube and Facebook, as well as Tuan Ibrahim’s Facebook account.
The suit involves claims of both slander and libel.

Title: Johor police bust drug syndicate supplying local market, seize RM8.49m worth of drugs
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — Johor police have busted a drug trafficking syndicate following the arrest of two men and the seizure of various types of drugs worth RM8.49 million in two separate raids in the Seri Alam area here on Wednesday (Aug 5).
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the raids were conducted at an apartment in Masai and a terrace house in Taman Ehsan Jaya at about 10.30 am.
He said the first raid, at the apartment, led to the arrest of a 30-year-old man believed to be the caretaker of a drug storage facility, while another 34-year-old man, believed to be an aide to the syndicate’s mastermind and responsible for paying the caretaker’s salary, was arrested at the terrace house.
“Upon inspecting the apartment, we seized 132,600 Erimin 5 pills, 53,000 ecstasy pills, 290 packets of ecstasy powder, 13 packets of ketamine and two packets of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, weighing 96.76 kg in total,” he told a press conference at the Johor Police Headquarters here today.
Police also seized for cars, namely a Honda City Hatchback, a Toyota Vellfire, a BMW M4 and a Proton Saga, as well as a EZI RAY 01 motorcycle and RM100,000 in cash.
He said the syndicate, which had been active in distributing drugs to the local market since May, used a guarded and gated apartment as a storage facility, adding that police were intensifying efforts to track down the syndicate’s mastermind.
The two suspects, who have previous criminal records, have been remanded for a week from Aug 6 and the case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs. Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Four-month-old baby girl’s death in Johor probed as murder, investigation papers sent to prosecution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Police have reclassified the death of a four-month-old baby girl in Taman Sri Saujana in Johor Bahru as murder, with the investigation papers referred to the Johor prosecution office for further action.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the investigation was initially conducted under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for neglect resulting in the baby’s death, before being reclassified under Section 302 of the Penal Code following a post-mortem.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Rahaman said the post-mortem conducted at Pasir Gudang Hospital on August 2 found that the baby died from trauma to the abdomen and chest caused by a blunt object.
He said the completed investigation papers were referred to the Johor prosecution office yesterday, while police had received instructions to charge the baby’s step-grandmother under Section 302 at the Kota Tinggi Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.
“We received instructions to charge the victim’s step-grandmother under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder at the Kota Tinggi Magistrates’ Court tomorrow,” he said at a press conference at the Johor police headquarters.
Rahaman said police had detained the step-grandmother, as well as the baby’s grandfather and mother, to assist in investigations, with all three remanded from August 2 until tomorrow.
He said police received a report from a 39-year-old woman on July 31 claiming that the baby had been found dead while sleeping at the house.
Medical personnel who arrived at the scene attempted to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation on the baby, but she was pronounced dead at 10.30am that day.
The baby had been under the care of her step-grandmother as her 18-year-old mother was still studying at college.

Title: Sarawak orders schools to halt outdoor activities amid unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Schools in Sarawak have been ordered to immediately halt all outdoor activities involving pupils in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100.
Sarawak Education Department director Omar Mahli said district education offices and educational institutions under the department had been reminded to prioritise the welfare, health and safety of pupils amid hot weather and haze,
Utusan Malaysia
reported today.
He said schools should postpone all outdoor activities if the weather was excessively hot and monitor activities that could expose pupils to such conditions to prevent their health from being affected.
“For areas recording API readings above 100, all outdoor activities involving pupils must be stopped,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Sarawak Education Department School Management Sector deputy director Dr Les Anak Met stressed the need for continuous monitoring of API readings in respective areas, as well as the management of outdoor and co-curricular activities according to API levels and current directives from the authorities.
He said the health and safety of pupils and school staff should also be prioritised, particularly those with health conditions such as asthma and other respiratory illnesses.
“Schools are also reminded to ensure clear and effective communication with parents, while district education offices must continuously monitor schools under their supervision and provide updates to the Sarawak Education Department,” he said.
All district education offices and schools have also been urged to remain vigilant about haze conditions in their respective areas, comply with authorities’ directives and take proactive action based on the prevailing situation.
Meanwhile, the 53rd Sarawak Schools Sports Council (MSSS) Athletics Championship 2026, scheduled from August 10 to 14 at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (Unimas) Stadium, has been postponed due to unhealthy API readings in Samarahan.
As of 2pm today, 11 areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, with the Serian IPD air quality monitoring station recording the highest reading at 190.
According to information on the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website, 10 other monitoring stations also recorded unhealthy readings, including Samarahan at 169, Kuching (165), Bintulu (159), Samalaju (155) and Mukah (154).
Sibu recorded an API reading of 154, Sri Aman (154), Sarikei (153), Miri (146) and the Industrial Training Institute (ILP) Miri (123), with all readings falling within the unhealthy category of between 101 and 200.

Title: Woman, 78, believed killed in crocodile attack while collecting river snails in Batu Niah
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 11 — A 78-year-old woman was killed after it was believed that she was snatched from her boat by a crocodile while out looking for river snails with her daughter near Jambatan Suai in Batu Niah, Miri on Tuesday.
The victim has been identified as Sambai Anggah.
According to the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba), Sambai and her 31-year-old daughter were searching for snails around a tributary connected to Sungai Suai when the incident occurred.
Her daughter, who was in the river about one metre away, witnessed the crocodile snare Sambai from the boat.
“The crocodile then dragged the victim about 10 metres away from the boat before releasing her after villagers surrounded it,” Bomba said in a statement.
Villagers later found Sambai’s body floating in the river before recovering it and taking it to a nearby wharf.
Bomba received the emergency call at 11.26am and dispatched five personnel from the Batu Niah fire station to the scene, located at a junction before Suai Bridge.
The team arrived at 11.58am and carried out monitoring at the scene, which was subsequently declared safe and under control.
The victim’s body was handed over to the police for further action before the operation ended at 1.45pm. — The Borneo Post

Title: Johor sets up special team to probe claims of Singapore waste dumped in Pontian
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has set up a special team to investigate claims that construction waste from Singapore is illegally dumped in Pontian.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the team was formed with an integrated approach to enable a comprehensive investigation into the allegations.
“The special team will involve several agencies, including local authorities, the police, district offices and also the Solid Waste Management Corporation (SWCorp).
“This is to ensure that allegations of illegal dumping can be identified and investigated thoroughly, including if the activities are stil taking place,” he told reporters after a visit to an illegal scrap recycling premise in Kampung Maju Jaya in Kempas here today.
Mohd Jafni was responding to claims that construction waste from Singapore had entered Johor and was dumped in Pontian.
He said any waste brought in from Singapore and dumped in Johor without the necessary permits or approvals should not be allowed.
“We will not compromise on the matter. We will take appropriate action based on the laws in force,” he said.
Mohd Jafni said authorities have received reports regarding the allegations that were detected in Sungai Karang, Pontian and several nearby areas, but they are still under investigation.
He said that if the probe finds that the activities are still occurring, an integrated enforcement team will be immediately mobilised.
“The state government will not compromise if there were parties who took advantage of Johor as a location for illegal waste disposal.
“An integrated enforcement action is important to ensure that the issue did not recur and to protect the interests of the people and environment.
Earlier, it was reported that DAP parliamentarian Lim Lip Eng called for accountability following a report alleging that a convoy of trailers from Singapore has been dumping construction waste in Pontian, Johor, for the past two years.
The Kepong MP questioned if there was any negligence involving enforcement and checks at the Singapore-Johor checkpoint if the report was true.

Title: Tabung Haji RCI: MPs call for transparent probe, accountability to protect depositors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Members of Parliament across the political divide today called for independent and transparent investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) after it was tabled in Parliament.
Despite the absence of PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara lawmakers, more than 30 MPs took part in the ongoing debate in the Dewan Rakyat.
Government backbenchers, led by Sekijang MP Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa, called on the government to clarify the involvement of TH’s leadership between 2014 and 2020 in negotiations over investments and allegations surrounding the matter.
Dr Zaliha also called on the government to publish a complete report on the progress of the 25 recommendations made by the RCI to restore depositors’ confidence in TH.
The government had previously said that 75 per cent of the recommendations had been implemented as of last month.
However, Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman called for a clear timeline for implementing the remaining 25 per cent of the recommendations, as well as details of the authorities responsible for the reforms.
Meanwhile, Bukit Bendera MP Syerleena Abdul Rashid said individuals identified in the report as being responsible for mismanagement and abuse of power should be prosecuted, regardless of their position or political affiliation.
“If no one is held responsible after this extensive report, then what is the message that we are sending out?” she asked.
Port Dickson MP Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said the practice of rewarding political loyalty with positions in TH should end and that the institution should be helmed by competent individuals.
On the opposition bench, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman called for the establishment of a multi-agency task force and a forensic audit into the 14 failed investments identified by the RCI.
Echoing the proposal, former prime minister and Pagoh MP Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin called for the independent forensic audit to be completed within a year.
The 252-page RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, was made public last month with the Cabinet’s approval.
A special Parliament sitting was convened today for lawmakers to debate the report.
The report found, among other things, non-compliance with accounting standards in declaring high dividends in 2017, unauthorised bonuses, as well as 14 troubled and failed investments.

Title: Appeal backfires as man’s sentence for causing two-month-old daughter’s death raised to 30 years
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — A man who appealed for a shorter prison sentence for causing the death of his two-month-old daughter instead had his sentence increased to the maximum 30 years by the Court of Appeal here today.
Justice Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, who delivered the decision of a three-member bench, said although the prosecution had not cross-appealed against the sentence, the court had the discretionary power under Section 60 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 (CJA)  to enhance Muhammad Daniel Iman Mohd Sharif’s sentence.
Also on the bench were Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah and K. Muniandy.
Justice Hayatul said the 16-year prison sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court did not reflect the seriousness of the offence and the violence involved.
The court set aside the 16-year prison sentence and substituted it with the maximum 30-year sentence under Section 304 (a) of the Penal Code, to run from the date of arrest on Aug 1, 2022.
In delivering the court’s decision, Justice Hayatul said the court had taen into consideration that the deceased was a two-month-old infant who was helpless and dependent on her parents for protection.
“Unfortunately, in the present case, the infant was instead subjected to abused (aniaya). It was not a one-off incident but rather repeated acts that were inhumane,” she said.
She said that on July 30, 2022, the infant’s mother heard her crying from the living room, where the appellant was also present.
Justice Hayatul said the appellant took the infant from a cushion which was on the floor and slammed her down, causing her to cry, adding that the following day, the appellant yanked the infant’s hand, pressed on her stomach and slammed her onto the cushion again, causing her head to hit the corner of a table, resulting in head injuries.
She said post-mortem report confirmed that the infant died from blunt trauma to the head.
Justice Hayatul said the appellant’s argument that the High Court had failed to take into consideration his young age was not commensurate with the violent nature of his conduct.
She further said the 30-year prison sentence would give the appellant time and opportunity to reflect on his cruel actions, reform himself and become a better person, while also serving as a warning to the appellant and society at large.
Earlier, Muhammad Daniel, through his counsel K.A. Ramu appealed for a shorter prison sentence, asking the court to consider that he was 21 years old at the time of the offence.
He said Muhammad Daniel, 25, was initially charged with murder, but the prosecution accepted his representation to reduce the charge under Section 304 (a) of the Penal Code, to which he pleaded guilty.
Deputy Public Prosecutor P. Sarulatha told the court that although there was no cross-appeal by prosecution against the sentence, the court could still increase the sentence under Section 60 of the CJA.
The Shah Alam High Court in May this year had sentenced Muhammad Daniel to 16 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of his infant daughter at his home in Bandar Tasik Puteri, Rawang, between July 30 and 31, 2022.
He has one final avenue of appeal with the Federal Court. — Bernama

Title: Man jailed two years for punching wife, attempting to murder her with car
Article:
KANGAR, Aug 12 — A man was sentenced to two years in prison by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to injuring and attempting to murder his wife in September last year.
Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid sentenced Mohd Hasmi Mohd Salleh, 39, to one year in prison for intentionally causing hurt to his wife and two years for attempting to murder her, with the sentences to run concurrently from the date of his arrest on Sept 21, 2025.
On the first charge, Mohd Hasmi was accused of punching his wife, Norzuraida Don Khodet, on her right arm, causing bruising. The charge was framed under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read with Section 326A, which provides for a maximum two-year prison sentence, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
He was also charged under Section 307 of the Penal Code with attempting to murder his wife by trying to hit her with a Proton Wira Aeroback, an offence punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a fine.
The offences were committed at 3.10 am and 3.25 am at Jalan Haji Hamid, Kampung Jelempok, Arau, on Sept 20, 2025. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji Act amendments to introduce tougher financial reporting rules, penalties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Clearer legal provisions, including prescribed accounting standards and penalties for misreporting financial statements, will be included in proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji (TH) Act 1995 to tighten financial reporting rules in line with recommendations by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the changes were intended to prevent a recurrence of the issues highlighted by the RCI in its report on TH management and operations from 2014 to 2020.
“All relevant RCI recommendations have been reviewed for inclusion in the proposed amendments to the TH Act, including the suitability of a Securities Commission oversight and supervisory framework for TH’s fund management and investments,” he said when presenting his ministerial briefing on the RCI report at the special Dewan Rakyat sitting today.
Zulkifli said a task force chaired by the TH chairman and comprising the Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) governor and Securities Commission (SC) chairman had been established to examine the matter.
“I have been informed that the task force has agreed to recommend that TH’s fund management and investment activities be regulated by the SC, while haj management would remain under the supervision of the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Religious Affairs. TH would remain a single, intact entity,” he said.
On excessive bonuses, forensic audits and enforcement, Zulkifli said the RCI had recommended ending the practice of awarding excessively high bonuses to staff.
He said TH has since adopted a more measured bonus policy based on its overall financial performance and the achievement of key performance indicators by the institution and its employees. The payments are subject to approval by the religious affairs and finance ministers.
The minister said TH had also implemented a recommendation requiring profit distribution rates to be announced on the basis of audited annual financial statements since 2022.
The measure was in line with the RCI’s call for clearer provisions governing the calculation of TH’s profit distributions. Its financial statements have also fully complied with the relevant accounting standards since 2018, he said.
Zulkifli said the RCI also recommended a comprehensive overhaul of the TH Act 1995, including specific eligibility criteria and expertise-based selection procedures for board members, as well as a prohibition on active politicians serving as chairman or board members.
“TH has implemented leadership appointments, including those of board members and management, based on integrity, capability and experience under ‘fit and proper’ criteria aligned with BNM’s framework,” he said.
“We actually have many capable, competent and trustworthy technocrats and individuals of integrity who can lead TH. The institution is now in a very strong position in terms of haj management, investments, finances and its overall operations,” he said.
Apart from the ministerial briefing, the special sitting was held to allow MPs to scrutinise and debate the 211-page report released publicly on July 29 after the government decided its findings should be disclosed.
Zulkifli and Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan are scheduled to wind up the debate later. — Bernama

Title: Johor orders Kempas scrap metal recycling premise to shut down over air pollution risk
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has ordered an illegal scrap metal recycling premise in Kampung Maju Jaya, Kempas, here, to shut down immediately following claims of air pollution.
The premise is also located near an underground gas pipeline owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), raising safety concerns for more than 10,000 residents in four nearby villages.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the closure order followed an investigation which found that the premise, which had been operating for more than five years, was involved in open burning activities.
He said an inspection found that the 3.4-hectare site was being used for activities not in line with the land’s status.
“Checks showed that the land is zoned for agricultural purposes.
“However, we believe that the premise is used as a collection point for various types of waste, including construction material, before being burned.
“So, even if the operator has a permit and licence, they have violated the land usage conditions,” he told reporters after visiting the premises in Jalan Kempas Lama-Seelong here today.
Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad, Johor Bahru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Ramdin Taha and Johor Solid Waste Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad.
Mohd Jafni said checks with the local authorities found that no licence had been issued to allow waste or scrap collection activities to be carried out at the site.
He said initial investigations found that the activity was believed to have been carried out by an entrepreneur who had been renting the land from its Singaporean owner for the past five years.
“The authorities need to locate the land’s owner because he rented this site to the entrepreneur.
“Investigators need to determine whether the owner had abetted the suspects or the activity was part of his business,” he said.
Radin Ramlan said the authorities were in the midst of locating the Singaporean landowner who allegedly rented out the site for a scrap metal recycling operation.
He said this was to facilitate an investigation after the land tenant and three Bangladeshi workers were arrested over allegations that they were involved in open burning activities.
“The four male suspects involved have since been remanded to assist in investigations, while authorities have also sealed the premise.
“The local tenant of the premises has been remanded for four days starting last Monday, while three Bangladeshi male workers have been remanded for 14 days starting yesterday until August 23,” he told reporters.
The premise is located about 150 metres from an underground gas pipeline owned by Petronas, initially raising concerns over safety in the event of a fire or explosion.
However, a technical inspection conducted by Petronas confirmed that the underground gas pipeline was in a safe condition.
Yesterday, Johor SWCorp said it had initiated an investigation paper into the failure of a land tenant to comply with a notice to remove controlled solid waste in Kampung Sinaran Baru, Kempas, here.
Johor SWCorp said the investigation was being conducted under Section 75 of the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Act 2007 (Act 672) and would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action.
Last Sunday, it was reported that about 10,000 residents from four villages around Kempas claimed they were affected by air pollution and faced the risk of an underground gas pipeline explosion from the illegal burning of scrap at the premise.

Title: Selangor seawater desalination plant feasibility study due by December
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A feasibility study on the development of a seawater desalination plant in Selangor is currently underway and is expected to be completed by December this year.
State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said Central Spectrum (M) Sdn Bhd, in collaboration with Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), had appointed a consultant to conduct the study, which was expected to take six months.
He said the study was among the state government’s efforts to diversify alternative water supply sources to meet development demands in the area, as well as reduce reliance on existing water treatment plants (LRAs).
“The study will assess the technical, economic and environmental aspects, as well as the overall feasibility of the project.
“At present, the overall cost has yet to be determined, although we have examined its viability… (this is because) in terms of implementation costs, the cost of the project has come down compared with previously. Similarly, solar systems used to be expensive, but prices are now relatively competitive,” he said.
He was responding to a question from Mu’izzuddeen Mahyuddin (PN-Hulu Bernam) on the latest status of the feasibility study on the construction of a seawater desalination plant to ensure a long-term alternative water source for Selangor at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Elaborating, Izham said several potential locations had been identified along the eastern coastline of Pulau Indah as suitable sites for the development of the plant and would be finalised based on the findings of the study.
Meanwhile, he said the current treated water production by Air Selangor stood at 5,450 million litres per day (MLD).
“Air Selangor projects that water supply demand will increase to 9,653 MLD by 2045. In this regard, alternative water supply sources are being studied to ensure a sustainable and reliable water supply for Selangor,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Najib returned US$620m after GE13 because he was uncomfortable holding it, High Court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The High Court here was told today that former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak returned US$620 million out of the US$681 million he received as a purported “Arab donation” because he was uncomfortable keeping such a large amount of money in his bank account.
Najib’s lead counsel, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said according to his client, the money was returned to the sender, Tanore Finance Corporation, after the 13th General Election (GE13) in 2013.
The veteran lawyer said that Najib returned the money to Tanore in the hope that it (Tanore) was part of the Arab donation.
Muhammad Shafee suggested this to an offshore asset recovery specialist, Angela Barkhouse, the managing director of Kroll (Cayman) Ltd and head of Kroll’s Offshore Practice, who is the third plaintiff witness, on the sixth day of the trial of 1MDB’s US$5.64 billion civil suit against Najib and six others.
Muhammad Shafee:
Now, isn’t that consistent with his (Najib’s) claim that he believed the money was an Arab donation?
Barkhouse:
I can’t comment on that.
Muhammad Shafee:
But you are aware that the US$620 million was returned to Tanore…almost as soon as the election was over in Malaysia?
Barkhouse:
I am not sure of the date of the election, so I can’t comment or confirm it.
Previously, it was reported that Tanore was controlled by Eric Tan Kim Loong, an associate of fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low.
Muhammad Shafee then said the tracing of the funds showed that, after the money was returned, its final destination did not lead back to Najib, which Barkhouse agreed with.
Meanwhile, in a separate criminal proceeding against Najib, 1MDB trial judge Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah ruled that evidence, including bank records and the money trail, showed that the US$681 million had actually been misappropriated from 1MDB.
1MDB and its subsidiaries — 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited — filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named Najib, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh, former chief operating officer Radhi Mohamad, former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Make public full report on Tabung Haji RCI reforms, recovery efforts, says Dr Zaliha
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A full report on the implementation of the 25 recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), along with a report on efforts to recover its losses, should be made public to restore depositors’ confidence, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa said.
The Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman and Sekijang MP said disclosure was important given TH’s role as a key institution for Malaysian Muslims, particularly in managing savings for the haj pilgrimage.
“I welcome the progress in implementing the RCI recommendations, but I believe the August House should be given a fuller picture of which recommendations have been completed and which remain in progress, including a timeline for those yet to be implemented.
“I therefore propose that the implementation status be presented. A report on the recovery of losses should also be made public, so people know what has been done, what is being done and what will be done to address these issues.”
She said this during the debate following a ministerial briefing on the RCI report at today’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting.
Zaliha focused her debate on three areas, namely TH’s financial position and profit distributions, its investments, and governance accountability.
She highlighted the RCI’s finding that political pressure ahead of a general election was a key factor behind TH’s financial crisis.
“Some often speak about Muslim unity. I have no issue with that call, but what is the point of unity if the trust placed by Muslims is mismanaged and we defend those involved in problematic decisions?
“We need to examine the role of TH’s leadership at the time, including its former chairman, Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim.
“Apart from chairing the board, he also held positions in several TH subsidiaries and related companies. I understand that although he was a non-executive chairman, he was heavily involved in negotiations over several investments,” she said.
Zaliha also called on the government to clarify the extent of that involvement and to confirm an allegation that cash held in accounts linked to the former chairman had at one point reached RM170 million.
The government announced the establishment of the RCI in 2021 and appointed its members on January 20, 2022. Its report was subsequently presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on August 30, 2022.
The 211-page RCI report was only recently made public. It detailed findings on management and operational weaknesses at TH between 2014 and 2020 and set out 25 recommendations for improvement.
As of July 30 this year, TH had implemented 75 per cent of the recommendations. — Bernama

Title: Seven-year-old Indonesian boy found drowned after falling into river in Subang Jaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A seven-year-old Indonesian boy who fell into a river while playing with friends near Matahari Supermarket in Persiaran Subang Indah in Subang Jaya yesterday was found drowned this morning.
The Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said in a statement that the boy was found at 10.59am by personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station and its Water Rescue Team (PPDA), Astro Awani reported.
“The victim’s body was found about three kilometres from the location where he was reported to have fallen into the river at 6.30pm yesterday.
“The victim’s body was brought to the Fire Control Centre at noon for identification by his parents,” it said.
The body was later handed over to police for further action and taken to Serdang Hospital, with the operation fully concluded at 12.20pm.
JBPM said it received an emergency call about the incident at 8.06pm yesterday, before personnel from the Subang Jaya station arrived at the scene at 8.16pm.
The search and rescue operation also involved PPDA personnel from the Shah Alam, Port Klang and KLIA fire and rescue stations, as well as personnel from the Puchong station.
It said the search area was extended for more than eight kilometres downstream due to the strong current, covering three sectors from the incident site towards Sri Muda and Sungai Kandis.
JBPM said rescuers also faced several challenges, including strong river currents, the risk of rain upstream that could increase the current’s speed, and several natural rapids that made it difficult for boats to manoeuvre.

Title: Fix deadline for RCI reports to be tabled in Parliament, says Tuaran MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be amended to set a deadline for Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) reports to be tabled in Parliament, Tuaran MP Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said today.
Wilfred said the tabling of RCI reports should not be left solely to the government’s discretion as the purpose of establishing such commissions was to present the truth to the people.
His proposal came after several lawmakers questioned the government’s decision to postpone the tabling of the RCI report on Lembaga Tabung Haji until 2026 although it had been completed in 2023.
“To me, the question is not why tabling of the report was delayed, but it should be on why the country’s legal system did not set a time period for the tabling of RCI reports in Parliament.
“So, the Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be empowered so that tabling of RCI reports in Parliament does not rest solely on discretions (of the government),” Wilfred said during the debate on the Tabung Haji RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Last month, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Cabinet had withheld the report to allow reforms within Tabung Haji to take place and prevent erosion of trust among its depositors.
The report was tabled today and is currently being debated in the Dewan Rakyat.

Title: Kelantan opens 63 investigation papers into illegal mining, encroachment
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 11 — A total of 63 investigation papers were opened in connection with encroachment and illegal mining activities in Kelantan from 2025 to June this year.
Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the figure resulted from 77 enforcement operations conducted in hotspots involving the Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli and Tanah Merah districts.
“The state government, through enforcement agencies, has intensified field action to curb such activities.
“Following the operations, 63 investigation papers were opened and submitted to the Prosecution Unit of the Kelantan Land and Mines Office (PTG) for further action,” he said.
He said this when replying to a question from Datuk Shaari Mat Hussain (PAS-Paloh) on the state government’s efforts to address encroachment and illegal mining activities at the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly sitting at Kompleks Kota Darulnaim here today.
Elaborating, Mohamed Fadzli said the authorities had also seized 65 excavators estimated to be worth RM15.8 million to cripple the logistical capacity of such activities.
Answering a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Syahbuddin Hashim (BN-Galas) on the possibility of middlemen, masterminds, organisers, protectors or parties benefiting from the activities, he said investigations would be conducted to identify those involved.
“Once we identify the activity as illegal, we will lodge a police report and open an investigation paper. We know who owns the land, so investigations will be conducted and if we obtain information, we will take action.
“The state government has also discussed with the authorities and PTG to review the penalties, particularly for repeat offences, so that stricter action can be taken,” he said. — Bernama
